BASIS FOR DETERMNING DUES
A.N.A. dues are based on the combined total of all U.S. Advertising Expenditures by the Member Company
including the parent company and all eligible subsidiaries and divisions -- for the most recent calendar year preceding
the A.N.A. membership anniversary date of the Member Company.
The term U.S. Advertising Expenditures includes: all U.S. expenditures for advertising in any and all media
whether national, regional, or local; all U.S. advertising production costs (personnel including talent, services
and materiel); all U.S. advertising commissions and fees; and the Member's share of all expenditures within
the U.s. for cooperative advertising programs. It includes such monies expended directily by the Member, as
well as those by other firms or entities by arrangement with the Member that promote the Member's name,
products, services, brands, or other subjects of trade (e.g. expenditures by franchisees, licensees, distributors,
dealers, or other agencies).
The term Media includes: newspapers; periodicals; yellow pages; radio; television or other electronic systems; class
and technical journals; business, farm and religious papers; car cards; posters and out-of-home advertising.
Billing for Members' dues shall be based on the best published data available to A.N.A. for such expenses. If a
Member's actual expenses are substantially lower than those reflected in the A.N.A. invoice, the Member shall have
the option to supply the Association with an amount for its total expenses certified by its Chief Financial Officer, and
to remit its dues based upon such certified amount.
Dues are based on estimated advertising expenditures of $_30, 000, 000
